concepts.def: Tajfel and Turner (1979): self-concept derives partly from group membership; in-group favouritism and out-group discrimination.
Bandura (1986): behaviour learned through observation, imitation and vicarious reinforcement; reciprocal determinism.
Steele and Aronson (1995) showed stereotype threat lowered African-American students' test scores by 12%.
Asch (1951) line study: 37% mean conformity to wrong group answer; rises with unanimity and group size up to 3.
Hofstede (1980): individualism vs collectivism dimension predicts conformity; collectivist cultures show higher rates.
Process of learning one's own culture; Fagot (1985) found parents reinforced gender-typed toys from age 2.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sociocultural Approach to Behaviour — a core area of Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sociocultural Approach to Behaviour brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sociocultural Approach to Behaviour.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
